key_insight: Ly and Gong propose that deep learning’s unpredictable outcomes arise from fractal basin geometry: starting points that lead to different outcomes are interwoven at arbitrarily fine scales. Increasing numerical precision may therefore offer little improvement in predictability.
problem_solved: Addresses why deep learning runs can produce different outcomes despite nearly identical starting conditions, making results difficult to predict and reproduce.
method: Frame training outcomes in terms of basins: sets of starting points that lead to particular outcomes.
Propose fractal interweaving of these basins as a mechanism for sensitivity to tiny differences in starting conditions.
Connect this geometry to limits on the benefits of increasing numerical precision.
impact: The proposed mechanism suggests that higher precision alone may not ensure reproducible training. For practitioners, it motivates evaluating variability across runs rather than relying on a single result.
visual_elements: Color-coded starting-point map, with each color representing a different training outcome.
Nested zoom panels showing different outcome regions remaining interwoven at finer scales.
Two nearly identical starting points with arrows leading to distinct outcomes.
Conceptual precision-versus-predictability chart illustrating limited gains, clearly labeled as schematic.
paper_title: Fractal basin geometry and the limits to predictability and reproducibility in deep learning
